title: A Randomized Trial of Intensive versus Standard Blood-Pressure Control
content: Real source PMID 26551272. The SPRINT randomized clinical trial compared intensive systolic blood pressure control below 120 mm Hg with standard control below 140 mm Hg in adults with systolic blood pressure at least 130 mm Hg and elevated cardiovascular risk. The trial excluded patients with diabetes and prior stroke. Intensive control lowered major cardiovascular events and all-cause mortality, but serious adverse events including hypotension, syncope, electrolyte abnormalities, and acute kidney injury or failure were more frequent. Relevant concepts: hypertension, high blood pressure, cardiovascular risk, stroke, heart failure, chronic kidney disease, CKD, adverse events, intensive treatment, diabetes exclusion.

title: Sodium-glucose co-transporter-2 inhibitors with and without metformin: A meta-analysis of cardiovascular, kidney and mortality outcomes
content: Real source PMID 33043620. This meta-analysis of event-driven randomized placebo-controlled SGLT2 inhibitor trials evaluated cardiovascular, kidney, heart failure, and mortality outcomes with and without baseline metformin use. SGLT2 inhibitors reduced major adverse cardiovascular events, hospitalization for heart failure or cardiovascular death, major kidney outcomes, and all-cause mortality, with consistent effects regardless of whether patients were receiving metformin. Relevant concepts: type 2 diabetes, diabetic kidney disease, chronic kidney disease, heart failure hospitalization, cardiovascular death, kidney outcomes, metformin, empagliflozin, dapagliflozin, canagliflozin, SGLT2 inhibitors.

title: Inhaled Corticosteroids for the Prevention of Asthma Exacerbations
content: Real source PMID 34400314. This review summarizes asthma exacerbation risk factors and the role of inhaled corticosteroids. It reports that inhaled corticosteroids are effective for preventing asthma exacerbations, with strategies including daily controller treatment, intermittent high-dose inhaled corticosteroids in selected patients, and as-needed inhaled corticosteroid dosing with rescue treatment in mild asthma. title: Bleeding Risk in Nonvalvular Atrial Fibrillation Patients Receiving Direct Oral Anticoagulants and Warfarin
content: Real source PMID 32676543. This systematic review and meta-analysis of observational studies compared bleeding risk in nonvalvular atrial fibrillation patients receiving direct oral anticoagulants and warfarin. Overall, direct oral anticoagulants were associated with fewer bleeding events than warfarin in observational data. Agent-specific findings differed: apixaban showed lower bleeding risk compared with warfarin, while rivaroxaban did not show the same reduction. Relevant concepts: atrial fibrillation, AF, anticoagulation, DOAC, NOAC, warfarin, apixaban, rivaroxaban, dabigatran, bleeding, stroke prevention.

title: 2024 ACC/AHA/Multisociety Guideline for Lower Extremity Peripheral Artery Disease: Key Points
content: Real source: 2024 ACC/AHA multisociety guideline key points for lower extremity peripheral artery disease. In symptomatic PAD, single antiplatelet therapy is recommended to reduce major adverse cardiovascular events; aspirin or clopidogrel can be used. In symptomatic PAD and after endovascular or surgical revascularization, low-dose rivaroxaban 2.5 mg twice daily combined with low-dose aspirin is recommended to reduce major adverse cardiovascular and limb events. Full-intensity oral anticoagulation should not be used solely to reduce PAD cardiovascular or limb events when there is no other indication such as atrial fibrillation. High-intensity statin therapy aiming for at least 50 percent LDL-C reduction is recommended. Cilostazol is recommended to improve claudication symptoms and walking distance but should not be used in congestive heart failure. Relevant concepts: peripheral artery disease, PAD, antiplatelet therapy, aspirin, clopidogrel, rivaroxaban, statin, lipid lowering, cilostazol, claudication, revascularization.
